deepdive.sec: Wealth & Asset Management (UHNI/HNI) — Financialization of Savings

bull_bear.body: Deploying capital into lending and asset-management businesses (expected to lift ROE from 19.4%). B&K acquisition integration (ESOP/exceptional costs flowing through). SARs of ~Rs 60 cr over 4 years as retention comp. No dividend specifics on call.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 1) **AMC lumpiness** — single institutional redemptions can turn net flows negative (as this quarter); global allocations to listed India equity muted 6-9 months. 2) **Retention drift** on the listed-AMC book (structural). 3) **Execution on cost-to-income** — must actually land the 100-150 bps FY27 improvement while hiring 30-40 RMs/yr. 4) **UBS collaboration** still early — unit economics deliberately undisclosed. 5) **Key-man / succession** — Bain step-back chatter around Karan Bhagat's tenure (he pushed back firmly). 6) **Carry volatility** quarter-to-quarter.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Karan Bhagat highly confident, granular and candid — walked through cost-to-income bridges, retention decomposition, flow colour and the "two-and-a-half advisor" framing without dodging. Addressed the succession question head-on ("answered it 125 times… all of 49… 90%+ invested financially"). Transparent that AMC flows were lopsided on one redemption and that PMS is structurally migrating. Slightly reluctant on UBS unit economics ("wait and see over six months"). Overall: credible, execution-focused, owner-operator tone.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The profit engine is shifting from AUM growth to cost-to-income + break-evens** — HNI and ET Money flipping to break-even, plus operating leverage, is what bridges 51% → 47% C-I, independent of market beta.
- **B&K is quietly becoming an annuity + cross-sell asset**, not just broking — 600+ corporate treasury relationships feed wealth/treasury/lending, and listed-equity brokerage (~Rs 75 cr/qtr) is being reframed as a low-lumpiness, 15-20%-growth line rather than a cyclical trade.
- **PMS is structurally shrinking into AIF/MF/SIF** — same clients, same strategies, better pooled vehicles; a mix headwind to reported PMS but not to economics.
- **Client-count, not AUM, is the "acid test"** management watches — >Rs 10 cr clients 2,000 → 4,000+ over 3 years, targeting 8-10,000, because wallet-share expansion compounds on top.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body: - Board approved an interim dividend of Rs 7.50 per share for the quarter, and the deck carries a dedicated 'Capital allocation & dividend history' section (header only; no supporting detail was extracted).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Wealth (UHNI):** anchor franchise; addressable 40,000-45,000 households; three vectors — wallet-share deepening, beyond top cities, first-choice post-monetization. Advisory ~30-35 bps, discretionary 40-45 bps, distribution 65-70 bps.
- **HNI:** ~60+ RMs across 12 locations, >Rs 5,000 cr AUM (from ~Rs 600 cr → Rs 4,000 cr last yr → Rs 5,100-5,200 cr now), 800+ clients at ~90 bps; digital-first feeder into UHNI (200,000+ household TAM); revenue recognized with a 12-month lag (~Rs 7-8 cr trail started).
- **Asset Management / alternates:** PE, private credit, real estate, infra, renewables, multi-asset + listed; AUM >Rs 1 lakh cr; broadening AIF/PMS/MF/SIF shelf. PMS structurally migrating into AIF/MF/SIF pooled structures.
- **Institutional equities (B&K):** 550+ mid/small-cap companies covered, 300+ institutional clients, >85% of broking from cash segment; access to 600+ corporate treasuries feeding cross-sell; combined listed-equity brokerage ~Rs 310-320 cr run-rate (was Rs 250-260 cr at deal close).
- **ET Money:** FY26 reset toward profitability; break-even targeted this year.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Advisory practice at scale is the moat** — "at scale to build an advisory practice with this retention has not been that easy… building a product model is easier, scaling it is tougher; on advisory the service model is tougher to build and even tougher to charge fees." Advisory clients cross-use the platform ~3x a distribution client (trust, GIFT City, lending, brokerage), so blended retention is "not dramatically different" despite lower headline advisory bps.
- **"Two-and-a-half advisor" positioning** — clients typically end with 2-2.5 advisors (from 4-5 at start); 360 ONE's ability to be in the core two is the durable relationship advantage.
- **Private-credit track record** — negligible-to-zero credit accidents over 7-8 years in the 10-15% buckets; regulator-enforced no-gated-redemption structure keeps the industry clean.

latest_quarter.body: Headline ARR retention 78 → ~73-74 bps: ~2-2.5 bps is carry recognition (mostly AMC), ~1-2 bps is business mix (advisory lower-yield than distribution; TBR seasonally softer in Q1-Q2). Per-line margins unchanged. The only structural retention drag is the pure listed-AMC book (~8-9% of revenue). Cost-to-income bridge from 50-51% → ~47%: driven by HNI + ET Money break-even + operating leverage — **not** by cutting UHNI hiring (stable UHNI C-I ~45%, +100-200 bps for perpetual expansion/ramp).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Total ARR AUM Rs 3.42 lakh cr (+19%; wealth +24.2%, AMC +8.2%, AMC crossed Rs 1 lakh cr). ARR net flows Rs 10,815 cr (wealth Rs 13,379 cr; AMC net negative on one redemption). ARR revenue Rs 614 cr (+20.3%), TBR Rs 208 cr (+37.3%), total revenue Rs 870 cr (+20%). C-I 51.3% (from 53.5%), PAT Rs 330 cr (+14.8%), tangible ROE 19.4%. Retention 74 bps (down ~4 bps: half carry, half mix). Rs 12-13 cr exceptional ESOP (B&K). Guidance set: FY27 net flows ~12-15% of opening ARR (~Rs 35-40k cr, 70:30-75:25 wealth); C-I -100-150 bps (Q4 exit ~49-49.5%); HNI + ET Money break-even this year; UBS ~$500-600M AUM exchange in ~1 yr; RMs → 350-400 / families → 9-10,000 (3 yrs); TBR → Rs 750-1,000 cr (2-3 yrs); SARs ~Rs 60 cr / 4 yrs.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: (1) did AMC net flows recover (product launches)? (2) C-I trajectory toward ~49-50% full-year; (3) HNI break-even + ET Money loss narrowing to break-even by Q4; (4) UBS funds actually launched both ways + first AUM exchanged; (5) B&K brokerage run-rate +15-20%; (6) ECM team full-strength (Oct-Dec) & first mandates; (7) retention holding 70-75 bps._

outlook.body:
- **Net flows:** ~12-15% of opening ARR AUM (~Rs 35-40,000 cr for FY27), split ~70:30 to 75:25 in favour of wealth.
- **Cost-to-income:** improve ~100-150 bps for full-year FY27; Q4 exit ~49-49.5% (desire is ~49-50% full-year exit).
- **HNI business:** break-even and "a little bit of profitability this year itself"; **ET Money** break-even by Q4FY27 (run-rate loss now ~Rs 3-4 cr/qtr ex-exit costs, ~Rs 6-7 cr this quarter).
- **UBS collaboration:** conservative ~$500-600M AUM to be exchanged both ways over ~a year (started Jan-Mar'26); funds launching both ways in the coming quarter.
- **RM count:** toward 350-400 senior RMs (adding ~30-40/yr over 3 yrs); **UHNI families 9-10,000 in 3 years** (from 4,100).
- **TBR / broking:** transaction+brokerage toward Rs 750-1,000 cr over 2-3 yrs (ECM ~15-20% of that); listed equity brokerage ~Rs 75 cr/qtr (Rs 310-320 cr annualized run-rate), growing 15-20%/yr; TBR to stay ~20-25% of revenue (rising in quality, not lumpiness).
- **Carry:** ~3-5 bps of AIF alternates AUM (~Rs 240 cr/yr on ~Rs 60,000 cr).
- **SARs:** newly announced ~12 lakh SARs → ~Rs 60 cr cost spread over 4 years, starting next quarter (once allotted).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

deepdive.thesis: A clean compounding quarter for India's premium UHNI/alternates franchise: total ARR AUM +19% to Rs 3.42 lakh cr (wealth +24.2%, AMC +8.2%), ARR revenue +20.3% and PAT +14.8% to Rs 330 cr, with cost-to-income already inching down (53.5% → 51.3%). The story is now three converging optionalities — HNI + ET Money reaching break-even this year, the B&K institutional-equities/ECM integration turning broking more annuity-like, and the UBS collaboration beginning to move money both ways — all layered on a structurally under-penetrated wealth market. Near-term optics: AMC net flows were negative on a single institutional redemption ($550-600M → $175-180M) and headline ARR retention slipped ~4 bps (half carry, half mix), but management insists per-line margins are intact.

(2) C-I trajectory toward ~49-50% full-year; (3) HNI break-even + ET Money loss narrowing to break-even by Q4; (4) UBS funds actually launched both ways + first AUM exchanged; (5) B&K brokerage run-rate +15-20%; (6) ECM team full-strength (Oct-Dec) & first mandates; (7) retention holding 70-75 bps._

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Deck frames the company as 'Built to generate sustainable, high-quality growth' operating on 'Two business lines, one integrated platform' spanning Wealth Management and Asset Management.
- 360 ONE Wealth is described as servicing 9,000+ families and corporates; 360 ONE Asset is positioned as a leader in Indian alternates (Private Equity, Credit and Real Assets).
- The company states it is 'becoming AI-native on our own governed platform.'

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Wealth (UHNI):** anchor franchise; addressable 40,000-45,000 households; three vectors — wallet-share deepening, beyond top cities, first-choice post-monetization. Advisory ~30-35 bps, discretionary 40-45 bps, distribution 65-70 bps.
- **HNI:** ~60+ RMs across 12 locations, >Rs 5,000 cr AUM (from ~Rs 600 cr → Rs 4,000 cr last yr → Rs 5,100-5,200 cr now), 800+ clients at ~90 bps; digital-first feeder into UHNI (200,000+ household TAM); revenue recognized with a 12-month lag (~Rs 7-8 cr trail started).
- **Asset Management / alternates:** PE, private credit, real estate, infra, renewables, multi-asset + listed; AUM >Rs 1 lakh cr; broadening AIF/PMS/MF/SIF shelf. PMS structurally migrating into AIF/MF/SIF pooled structures.
- **Institutional equities (B&K):** 550+ mid/small-cap companies covered, 300+ institutional clients, >85% of broking from cash segment; access to 600+ corporate treasuries feeding cross-sell; combined listed-equity brokerage ~Rs 310-320 cr run-rate (was Rs 250-260 cr at deal close).
- **ET Money:** FY26 reset toward profitability; break-even targeted this year.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not an order-book business — pipeline = flow momentum + product launches. ARR net flows Rs 10,815 cr (wealth Rs 13,379 cr the driver); "a lot of product launches planned for the next 6-9 months" to balance wealth vs AMC flows. Alternates AUM ~Rs 58-60,000 cr; AMC AUM crossed Rs 1 lakh cr. Clients with >Rs 10 cr grew from ~1,800-2,000 (36 months ago) to >4,000. ECM/IB team building (4 coverage + process/compliance hires) — full-strength by Oct-Dec 2026, pitching actively from ~Jan 2027.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Net flows:** ~12-15% of opening ARR AUM (~Rs 35-40,000 cr for FY27), split ~70:30 to 75:25 in favour of wealth.
- **Cost-to-income:** improve ~100-150 bps for full-year FY27; Q4 exit ~49-49.5% (desire is ~49-50% full-year exit).
- **HNI business:** break-even and "a little bit of profitability this year itself"; **ET Money** break-even by Q4FY27 (run-rate loss now ~Rs 3-4 cr/qtr ex-exit costs, ~Rs 6-7 cr this quarter).
- **UBS collaboration:** conservative ~$500-600M AUM to be exchanged both ways over ~a year (started Jan-Mar'26); funds launching both ways in the coming quarter.
- **RM count:** toward 350-400 senior RMs (adding ~30-40/yr over 3 yrs); **UHNI families 9-10,000 in 3 years** (from 4,100).
- **TBR / broking:** transaction+brokerage toward Rs 750-1,000 cr over 2-3 yrs (ECM ~15-20% of that); listed equity brokerage ~Rs 75 cr/qtr (Rs 310-320 cr annualized run-rate), growing 15-20%/yr; TBR to stay ~20-25% of revenue (rising in quality, not lumpiness).
- **Carry:** ~3-5 bps of AIF alternates AUM (~Rs 240 cr/yr on ~Rs 60,000 cr).
- **SARs:** newly announced ~12 lakh SARs → ~Rs 60 cr cost spread over 4 years, starting next quarter (once allotted).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: 1) **UBS global collaboration** — offshore distribution for alternates/listed + NRI/resident/global cross-referrals. 2) **HNI feeder** into UHNI at scale. 3) **B&K ECM/IB** build-out (mandates from ~Jan 2027). 4) **Private credit** — management sees it growing as fast as PE over time (they operate the 10-11% and 13-15% buckets, "negligible to zero accidents" over 7-8 yrs). 5) **Migration of ~4,000 sub-scale (Rs 1-10 cr) clients** into the HNI servicing model over the next 3 months.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Headline ARR retention 78 → ~73-74 bps: ~2-2.5 bps is carry recognition (mostly AMC), ~1-2 bps is business mix (advisory lower-yield than distribution; TBR seasonally softer in Q1-Q2). Per-line margins unchanged. The only structural retention drag is the pure listed-AMC book (~8-9% of revenue). Cost-to-income bridge from 50-51% → ~47%: driven by HNI + ET Money break-even + operating leverage — **not** by cutting UHNI hiring (stable UHNI C-I ~45%, +100-200 bps for perpetual expansion/ramp).

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Deploying capital into lending and asset-management businesses (expected to lift ROE from 19.4%). B&K acquisition integration (ESOP/exceptional costs flowing through). SARs of ~Rs 60 cr over 4 years as retention comp. No dividend specifics on call.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Karan Bhagat highly confident, granular and candid — walked through cost-to-income bridges, retention decomposition, flow colour and the "two-and-a-half advisor" framing without dodging. Addressed the succession question head-on ("answered it 125 times… all of 49… 90%+ invested financially"). Transparent that AMC flows were lopsided on one redemption and that PMS is structurally migrating. Slightly reluctant on UBS unit economics ("wait and see over six months"). Overall: credible, execution-focused, owner-operator tone.

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position (OPTIONAL)
moat.body:
- **Advisory practice at scale is the moat** — "at scale to build an advisory practice with this retention has not been that easy… building a product model is easier, scaling it is tougher; on advisory the service model is tougher to build and even tougher to charge fees." Advisory clients cross-use the platform ~3x a distribution client (trust, GIFT City, lending, brokerage), so blended retention is "not dramatically different" despite lower headline advisory bps.
- **"Two-and-a-half advisor" positioning** — clients typically end with 2-2.5 advisors (from 4-5 at start); 360 ONE's ability to be in the core two is the durable relationship advantage.
- **Private-credit track record** — negligible-to-zero credit accidents over 7-8 years in the 10-15% buckets; regulator-enforced no-gated-redemption structure keeps the industry clean.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: 1) **AMC lumpiness** — single institutional redemptions can turn net flows negative (as this quarter); global allocations to listed India equity muted 6-9 months. 2) **Retention drift** on the listed-AMC book (structural). 3) **Execution on cost-to-income** — must actually land the 100-150 bps FY27 improvement while hiring 30-40 RMs/yr. 4) **UBS collaboration** still early — unit economics deliberately undisclosed. 5) **Key-man / succession** — Bain step-back chatter around Karan Bhagat's tenure (he pushed back firmly). 6) **Carry volatility** quarter-to-quarter.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The profit engine is shifting from AUM growth to cost-to-income + break-evens** — HNI and ET Money flipping to break-even, plus operating leverage, is what bridges 51% → 47% C-I, independent of market beta.
- **B&K is quietly becoming an annuity + cross-sell asset**, not just broking — 600+ corporate treasury relationships feed wealth/treasury/lending, and listed-equity brokerage (~Rs 75 cr/qtr) is being reframed as a low-lumpiness, 15-20%-growth line rather than a cyclical trade.
- **PMS is structurally shrinking into AIF/MF/SIF** — same clients, same strategies, better pooled vehicles; a mix headwind to reported PMS but not to economics.
- **Client-count, not AUM, is the "acid test"** management watches — >Rs 10 cr clients 2,000 → 4,000+ over 3 years, targeting 8-10,000, because wallet-share expansion compounds on top.
